KDT.design: Deep bass-baritone voice of a German man of about 38, a tank commander. Very low pitched, dark chest resonance, slightly gravelly. Calm authority: short, dry, clipped commands, firm and level. Native German speaker, no accent, close microphone.

RS.design: Low, dark baritone voice of a German man of about 27, a tank gunner. Quiet, focused and precise, terse replies, steady and level, very little melody. Native German speaker, no accent, close microphone.

LS.design: Low-pitched, rough and slightly hoarse voice of a young German man of about 21, a tank loader. Short, loud, blunt reports, breathy from physical work, but the voice stays low. Native German speaker, no accent, close microphone.

FA.design: Very deep, slow, gravelly bass voice of a German man of about 33, a tank driver. Laconic and matter-of-fact, heavy and unhurried. Native German speaker, no accent, close microphone.

FU.design: Low, even baritone voice of a German man of about 29, a radio operator. Clear crisp articulation, measured and businesslike, slightly nasal. Native German speaker, no accent, close microphone.

delivery.calm: He speaks calmly at a steady moderate pace, level intonation, low in his voice.
delivery.urgent: He speaks fast, hard and clipped with urgent force, like an order in combat, but his voice stays deep and low: no rise in pitch, no shouting high, no panic, controlled.

reference_text: Kiebitz an alle. Wir stehen am Waldrand, die Sicht nach Osten ist frei. Munition reicht, der Motor läuft ruhig.

lines.de: Richtschütze! Panzer, zwo Uhr, achthundert, am Waldrand.
lines.en: Gunner! Tank, two o'clock, eight hundred, at the edge of the woods.

lines.de: Panzer, drei Uhr, nah! Turm rechts, schnell!
lines.en: Tank, three o'clock, close! Turret right, quick!

lines.de: Zu kurz. Hundert mehr, gleiches Ziel.
lines.en: Short. Add one hundred, same target.
Hit up front! The plate is holding.

lines.de: Adler von Kiebitz: ein Feindpanzer abgeschossen.
lines.en: Adler from Kiebitz: one enemy tank knocked out.
Hit front left! The radio is out!

wording: ours: plausible Wehrmacht tank-crew intercom German, not from a period source
